title: epan: Define ENC_TIME_WINDOWS and use it
description:
Implement Windows FILETIME[1] as a ENC_TIME_WINDOWS encoding, so
that proto_tree_add_item() can use it. Use it in file-zip for the
NTFS extra field, as well as in the Procmon and Netmon dissectors.
There's a few cases that should use time_value_strings.

Note that a FILETIME is a 64-bit struct consisting of two 32-bit values,
with the low 32 bits first. That doesn't make a difference when retrieving
Little Endian (as our accessors deal with unaligned memory fine), but
makes a difference in Big Endian. Cf. ENC_TIME_NTP and ENC_TIME_RTPS
and how they handle Little Endian, vs ERF's interpretation of what a Little
Endian NTP-style timestamp should be.

In rare cases, Microsoft specs store a FILETIME value in a 64-bit
integer, as in "LARGE_INTEGER PasswordLastSet;" in [MS-SAMR][2]

The same value is seen in epan/dissectors/pidl/samr/samr.idl
as "NTTIME_hyper last_password_change;"

Those, implemented as dissect_nttime_hyper in packet-windows-common.h,
MUST NOT use this encoding along with ENC_BIG_ENDIAN; conversely,
dissect_nttime MAY use this encoding for ENC_BIG_ENDIAN.

[1] - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/minwinbase/ns-minwinbase-filetime
[2] - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-samr/1cd138b9-cc1b-4706-b115-49e53189e32e

notes.body: enabled automatic add to merge train when checks pass
Would `ENC_TIME_FILETIME` or `ENC_TIME_WINDOWS_FILETIME` more directly indicate what it is?
It might, though I think I would want to keep `WINDOWS` in there for the same reason we went away from `ENC_TIME_TIMESPEC` and `ENC_TIME_TIMEVAL`. I am very open to switching it.
